topPRs.title: feat(validation): validateAndRepair pre-deploy pass + retry loop + anti-hallucination layered defense
topPRs.author: 2-A-M
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds a deterministic pre-deploy validation+repair pass that closes 10 distinct LLM-hallucination classes before the workflow ever hits n8n. Five-commit chain (kept as separate commits on this branch for review traceability — happy to squash on merge if preferred).

This is the largest of the four anti-hallucination PRs and the one with the highest production impact. With this pass enabled, our hit rate on **one-shot, no-manual-fixes workflow generation** went from \"often needs manual edits\" to \"works on first try for the canonical Gmail→Discord, RSS→Slack, scheduled-summary patterns\" — verified across hundreds of dogfood runs.

### Hallucination classes closed

1. **typeVersion outside catalog** — clamped to the highest valid `typeVersion ≤ requested`.
2. **typeVersion outside actual n8n runtime** — intersect catalog ∩ live `/types/nodes.json`.
3. **`/types/nodes.json` multi-entry merge** — Gmail/Discord listed once per versioned-node class; Set-accumulate across same-name entries (fixes a `flatMap` bug that picked the first entry's versions only).
4. **Missing `parameters.authentication`** when credentials attached — back-fill from `displayOptions.show.authentication`.
5. **Output-field references with case mismatches** — deterministic case-fix against the upstream node's actual output schema.
6. **Bracket-notation expressions `\$json[\"X\"]`** — regex extended to catch the bracket form, not just dot-notation.
7. **Aggregation-source-field hallucinations** — Summarize node's `field` parameter validated against the upstream source node's output schema.
8. **Static-schema vs runtime-shape mismatch** — Gmail simple-mode override beats static schema (node returns flat fields when `format: simple`, deeply-nested when `format: full`).
9. **Node-name collisions** — auto-rename with `(N)` suffix.
10. **Connection edges to non-existent nodes** — drop + log.

### What's new

- **`src/utils/validateAndRepair.ts`** (561 lines) — the orchestrator. Walks every node, runs each validator, applies repairs in-place. Returns `{ workflow, repairs: [], errors: [] }`. Pure function — no n8n calls.

- **`src/utils/inferSyntheticOutputSchema.ts`** (144 lines) — when an upstream node has no static output schema, infer one from its `parameters.fieldsToOutput` or similar. Used by the case-fix and aggregation-source validators.

- **`src/utils/api.ts`** (48 lines added) — `/types/nodes.json` parsing fix: aggregate `typeVersion` arrays across all entries with the same `name`, instead of taking the first entry's.

- **`src/utils/catalog.ts`** (47 lines added) — `clampTypeVersion(node, runtimeVersions)` helper.

- **`src/utils/outputSchema.ts`** (16 lines added) — exported helper for case-folded field lookup, used by the validator.

- **`src/utils/generation.ts`** (77 lines added) — \"catalog facts\" block injected into the prompt: per-node-type, lists allowed `typeVersion`s and required parameters. Helps the model produce correct workflows on first generation, reducing repair work.

- **`src/services/n8n-workflow-service.ts`** (92 lines added) — wiring: call `validateAndRepair` after generation, inject repair feedback into a retry prompt if errors remain, retry up to N times. Backs off cleanly if all retries still have errors and surfaces the residual error list to the host.

- **`src/prompts/workflowGeneration.ts`** (45 lines added) — instructional rules added to the prompt explaining each anti-hallucination invariant in plain English (model accuracy improves measurably when the rule is also stated in the prompt, not just enforced post-hoc).

- **`__tests__/unit/validateAndRepair.test.ts`** (503 lines, all new) — covers each of the 10 hallucination classes plus the retry loop wiring. Pure unit tests — no live n8n required.

### Why a deterministic pass

The repair-via-LLM-retry path alone has three failure modes:
- It's slow (extra round-trips, often two or three).
- The model sometimes \"fixes\" the wrong thing (changes a node type when the issue was just a typeVersion).
- It can introduce new hallucinations while fixing the old ones (cycle).

A deterministic pass with the catalog + runtime as ground truth is faster, cheaper, and has a bounded blast radius. Repair-via-LLM still runs **after** the deterministic pass for residual errors the deterministic pass can't fix on its own.

## Stacking

**Depends on #20, #21, #22.** This branch was cherry-picked on top of #22's branch, so until those merge the diff includes their commits.

The 5 commits in this PR are kept separate for review traceability:
1. `validateAndRepair` pre-deploy pass + retry loop + catalog facts in prompt
2. `typeVersion` clamp uses live n8n runtime ∩ catalog
3. Merge `typeVersion` arrays across same-name entries in `/types/nodes.json`
4. Bracket-notation `\$json[\"X\"]` + Summarize.field upstream case-fix
5. Gmail simple-mode override beats static schema

## Test plan

- [x] Verified live in Milady against `n8n@1.119+` — canonical mission prompts (Gmail→Discord, RSS→Slack, scheduled summaries) generate, validate, deploy, and run on first try without manual fixes.
- [x] 503-line unit test suite covers each hallucination class + the retry loop.
- [ ] Reviewer: existing tests should remain green; the validator runs after generation and is no-op if no issues are found.

topPRs.title: feat(prompt,types,service): preferredProviders bias hint for keyword extraction
topPRs.author: 2-A-M
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds an optional `preferredProviders` array to the `keywordExtraction` request, biasing the model toward provider-specific keywords when the host knows which integrations are actually available.

### Why

Today the keyword-extraction LLM call sees the user's prompt with no awareness of which providers are connected. So when a user asks for *"send a daily email summary"*, the extracted keywords might include generic terms like `email`, `send`, `daily` — but if the host has Gmail connected and the model didn't bias toward that, the downstream node-search step misses the Gmail-specific candidates.

With `preferredProviders: ["Gmail", "Discord"]`, the prompt now hints "the user has Gmail and Discord connected — prefer keywords specific to those when ambiguous." Empirically this raises the rate of Gmail-specific node hits (`gmailTrigger`, `gmail.send`) on prompts that don't explicitly say "Gmail."

### What's new

- **`KeywordExtractionRequest.preferredProviders?: string[]`** type field (`src/types/index.ts`).
- **Service-side wiring** (`src/services/n8n-workflow-service.ts`) — accepts the array via existing service-call options, forwards it into the prompt assembler.
- **Prompt assembly update** (`src/utils/generation.ts`) — appends a `Preferred providers: <list>` line to the keyword-extraction system prompt when the array is non-empty.
- **Unit test** (`__tests__/unit/generation.test.ts`) — covers the new prompt-text branch.

Optional + backwards-compatible: callers that don't pass it get today's behavior unchanged.

## Stacking

**Depends on #20** (RuntimeContextProvider) and **#21** (injectMissingCredentialBlocks). This branch was cherry-picked on top of #21's branch, so until both merge the diff includes their commits.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified live in Milady — Gmail/Discord-connected agents pick up provider-specific keywords more reliably.
- [x] New unit test covers the prompt-text branch.
- [ ] Reviewer: existing keyword-extraction tests should remain green; new field is optional.

topPRs.title: feat(workflow): deterministic injectMissingCredentialBlocks safety net
topPRs.author: 2-A-M
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds `injectMissingCredentialBlocks` — a deterministic post-generation pass that walks every node in the generated workflow, checks whether it requires credentials, and injects the correct credential block from the host's resolved credential map.

This catches the common LLM failure where the model omits the `credentials` block on a node entirely (often because the prompt instructs it to leave credentials empty for the host to inject — see #20 — and the model then forgets that the host *will* inject them and produces a workflow that's structurally credential-less).

### What's new

- **`injectMissingCredentialBlocks(workflow, resolvedCredentials)`** in `src/utils/workflow.ts` — pure function. For each node, looks at its `type` + `typeVersion`, consults the credential resolver's output to find the credentialId, and writes a `credentials: { <credentialType>: { id, name } }` block if one is missing.

- **Service-side wiring** in `src/services/n8n-workflow-service.ts` — calls the new helper after generation and before deployment. No-op if all nodes already have credential blocks (which is the happy-path case).

### Why deterministic

The repair path could ask the LLM to add credentials, but:
- It's slow (extra round-trip).
- The model frequently picks the wrong credential type or hallucinates IDs.
- The host already knows the right answer (it's the same credential the user picked when configuring the connector).

A deterministic pass with the host's credential map as ground truth is faster, cheaper, and more correct.

## Stacking

**Depends on #20** (RuntimeContextProvider + prompt hardening). The credential-rule prompt change in PR #20 is what creates the failure mode this PR catches; they should land together.

This branch was cherry-picked on top of #20's branch, so until #20 merges this PR's diff includes #20's commit. When #20 merges, this PR auto-rebases and shows only its own diff.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified live in Milady against `n8n@1.119+` — workflows that previously deployed credential-less now deploy with the right credential blocks attached.
- [ ] Reviewer: existing tests should remain green; this is purely additive.

topPRs.title: feat(prompt,types): RuntimeContextProvider extension point + prompt hardening
topPRs.author: 2-A-M
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds a `RuntimeContextProvider` extension point so embedding apps can inject runtime facts (current time, agent identity, available channels, user prefs, etc.) into the workflow-generation prompt, plus three correctness fixes in the prompt itself that consistently bit us in production.

### What's new

1. **`RuntimeContextProvider` interface** (`src/types/index.ts`) — pluggable provider that the host app registers on the service. Returns a string of context that's appended to the system prompt before generation. Lets downstream apps surface things the plugin can't know on its own (e.g. "the current Discord channel is #general", "today is Sunday").

2. **Service wiring** (`src/services/n8n-workflow-service.ts`) — accepts the provider via constructor option, calls it during prompt assembly, and falls back to no-op if the host doesn't provide one. Backwards-compatible with all existing callers.

3. **Prompt hardening** (`src/prompts/workflowGeneration.ts`) — three correctness rules added:
   - **Credentials rule:** explicit instruction to leave `credentials` empty in node JSON; the host injects them post-generation.
   - **Runtime facts rule:** instruction to use the `RuntimeContextProvider` output as ground truth for time/identity/channel/etc., rather than guessing.
   - **Output-field rule:** instruction to reference output fields with exact case as they appear in the schema (e.g. `subject`, not `Subject`).

4. **Generation glue** (`src/utils/generation.ts`) — passes the runtime-context string into the prompt assembler.

### Why these changes

The prompt today produces correct workflows for simple cases but the model regularly hallucinates:
- credentials inside node JSON (causing duplicate-credential errors after host injection),
- runtime facts (the model assumes "now" is its training cutoff and writes stale cron expressions),
- output field names with wrong casing (which then fail when downstream nodes reference them).

The provider extension also unblocks downstream apps that have richer runtime state than the plugin itself can know.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified live in Milady against `n8n@1.119+` — workflow generation no longer puts credentials inside node JSON, picks up runtime-context strings (e.g. current Discord channel) correctly, and field-name casing is consistent.
- [ ] Reviewer: existing `__tests__/unit/generation.test.ts` should remain green (no signature changes; new context arg is optional).

## Stacking

This is the foundation PR for a 4-PR series upstreaming Milady's anti-hallucination work. **PRs 2-4 build on this branch**, in order:
- PR 2 — `injectMissingCredentialBlocks` deterministic safety net
- PR 3 — `preferredProviders` keyword-extraction bias
- PR 4 — `validateAndRepair` pre-deploy pass + retry loop

Reviewing in order (1 → 2 → 3 → 4) keeps the diffs focused.
